carousels.name: What a just-once relapse really costs

slides.title: The relapse you're planning for "just once" [[will cost you more than one night.]]
slides.sub: What a mid-month p*rn relapse really looks like.

slides.title: "Just [[once]]"
slides.body: You tell yourself it's one p*rn session. Then it's two hours.

slides.title: The "[[screw it]]" day
slides.body: Streak's gone anyway. Many people describe binging p*rn even harder the next day.

slides.title: The [[slide]]
slides.body: Old habits come back fast. Phone in bed. Late nights. The guilt loop. 15 days undone in a week.

slides.title: You're not a "high sex drive" guy. [[You're a high p*rn habit guy.]]
slides.sub: There's a difference. And it matters.

slides.title: Drive vs. [[habit]]
slides.body: A strong drive wants connection and real intimacy. A p*rn habit wants a screen, alone, at 1 AM. Those aren't the same thing.

carousels.name: Most people with p*rn problems never get help

slides.title: 90%+ of people with a p*rn problem [[never get help.]] Don't be one of them.
slides.sub: What the International Sex Survey found.

slides.title: Sought [[treatment]]
slides.body: In the International Sex Survey (Bőthe et al., 2024), only 4–10% of people with problematic p*rn use had ever sought treatment. That means 90% or more never did.

slides.title: Why [[men]] wait
slides.body: "I should handle this myself." "It's embarrassing." "It's not that bad yet." Waiting is how "not that bad" becomes years.

slides.title: Help isn't [[weakness]]
slides.body: You'd see a coach for fitness or a mentor for your career. P*rn addiction deserves the same seriousness.
